links.comparator_used: EHR-alone (single-modality structured EHR) baseline and unimodal baselines
links.outcome: 30-day COPD readmission discrimination (ROC-AUC) and calibration (Brier score) after recalibration
links.effect: No fusion architecture significantly outperformed EHR-alone (ROC-AUC 0.63); non-EHR modalities alone had ROC-AUC 0.46-0.53; after recalibration Brier was EHR-alone 0.239 vs fusion 0.240-0.244, with all paired bootstrap 95% CIs including zero
links.quote: No fusion architecture significantly outperformed the EHR-alone baseline (ROC-AUC 0.63); removing auxiliary modalities improved rather than degraded fusion performance under stress testing.

links.comparator_used: Raw, uncalibrated probabilities from the EHR-alone probe and the fusion models
links.outcome: Brier score and calibration of EHR-alone predictions
links.effect: Raw EHR-alone Brier about 0.32 (calibration slope 0.12) vs fusion about 0.24; after logistic recalibration fitted on the validation set, EHR-alone Brier was 0.239 and fusion 0.240-0.244, indistinguishable
links.quote: The raw Brier score was lower for all three fusion architectures than for EHR-alone (about 0.24 versus 0.32), but this reflected overconfidence of the EHR-alone probe (calibration slope 0.12); after logistic recalibration fitted on the validation set, Brier scores were indistinguishable (EHR-alone 0.239; fusion 0.240-0.244; all paired bootstrap 95% CIs included zero).
